messages.subject: pie nodes
parts:
Multicolor Nodes, the plugin, could be good - but it doesn't work with
Cytoscape 2.8.1. I got a bunch of java errors on the Terminal and
gave up on it's failure to graph pie graph nodes.

Using RCytoscape, I solved the pie nodes problem by plotting pie
graphs in R and saving them as .png files, then sending the pie graphs
to Cytoscape as node images using the RCytoscape command
setNodeImageDirect(). This is good, except for the dissatisfying blank
square that surrounds each node (see attached). I can make
transparent the background of the R-generaged pie graph, but the image
loaded is still square. It doesn't seem to matter if I crop the image
of each pie.png, or setNodeOpacityDirect to 0 or setDefaultNodeColor
to 'transparent'. Edges that originate from the nodes do so too far
away, but those that cross the nodes do so as if the box is transparent

I had to setNodeLabelDirect after SetNodeImageDirect, not sure why,
the pie png goes on top of the label I guess.

Is there a way to draw the edges that originate from image nodes top
of the square png images? Or extend them?

Thanks,

Mark Grimes
University of Montana
ty of Montana

Hi Mark, 

you should be able to overwrite the visual attributes using the 
'overrideNodeVizAttribute' of CytoscapeRPC, though I don't know if

set this way, it won't be overwritten by a vizmap.

when a new network is loaded?

messages.subject: Re: [Cytoscape-discuss] pie nodes
parts:
Giuseppe

Nice way to make pie nodes.  We are doing something similar.  I am plotting nodes that have the presence or absence of up to four attributes.  I called the absence 'NA' in R and zero in Cytoscape.  

Gene att.1 att.2 att.3 att.4
A 1 1 0 0
B 0 0 0 1
C 1 1 1 1
D 0 1 1 1
...
I should be possible to construct a table like what you proposed from the above data, but I was able to accomplish pies cut appropriately in halfs, thirds or quarters from the data as above in the following way.  In R:

pi_cols <- c("green", "deepskyblue", "magenta", "gold")
cytoscape.file <- read.table(Filename, header=TRUE, sep = "\t", na.strings = "NA", fill=TRUE) # files in format above
rownames(cytoscape.file)  <- cytoscape.file$Gene.Name
cf  <- cytoscape.file[,c(2:5)]
names(cf)  <- pi_cols
setwd(genelist[i])
for (j in 1:nrow(cf)) {
png (filename = paste(rownames(cf[j,]), noquote("_pie.png"), sep="", collapse=NULL), type = "quartz", bg="transparent") 
pie ( as.vector(cf[j,!is.na(cf[j,])], mode= "integer"), labels =NA, radius= 1, col = names(cf)[!is.na(cf[j,])], border= "transparent", clockwise=T, init.angle = 0) 
dev.off() }
setwd("..")  
}

The commands plot pie graphs for all genes and save them in a subdirectory.  The attribute names are changed to colors that can be fed into pie(), which graphs are plotted with maximum radius (1) and no borders or labels.  The png() command followed by dev.off() is what saves the file.
 
Then using RCytoscape commands:

setwd(genelist[k])
pngfiles=list.files()
setNodeImageDirect(new.window, as.character(cf2[, 1]), sprintf ('file://%s/%s', getwd (), pngfiles))
setDefaultNodeColor (new.window, 'transparent') 
setNodeOpacityDirect (new.window, as.character(cf2[, 1]), 0)
setNodeLabelOpacityDirect (new.window, as.character(cf2[, 1]), 220)
setNodeLabelDirect (new.window, as.character(cf2[, 1]), as.character(cf2[, 1])) # is necessary, not sure why
setNodeShapeDirect (new.window, as.character(cf2[, 1]), 'vee') # better than "RECT" or "ellipse"
#
redraw(new.window)


This sets the directory to the one containing the pie graphs and places them into each node.  The node labels go away so they must be restored by force using setNodeLabelDirect (), presumably because they are overwritten (not sure why).  

Two problems remain. One is that the pie image is smaller than the node shape, which can be somewhat worked around using the shape 'vee' which has a smaller footprint. Basically the problem is to have the pie image fill the node shape entirely, which, if possible, would make the method I describe here generally useful.  Also, though this method works for plotting in Cytoscape, if the .cys file is saved and reopened Cytoscape gives visual.parser and other errors because it can't find the custom graphics.  I don't know how to embed the graphs in the .cys file.

Mark


On Aug 25, 2011, at 4:32 AM, Giuseppe G. wrote:

Hi,

If I understand correctly you're trying to do something similar to what I'm doing. I have a .noa file structured as follows

gene1 k
gene2 p
gene3 o
gene4 kp
gene5 ko
gene6 po
gene7 kpo

therefore I have say 3 attributes that can combine combinatorially for each node. Some will only be k, some both k & and p, etc.

I use the multicolour nodes to associate a colour to each of k, p, o. Say black for o, grey for k and red for p.

What the plugin then allows me to do is to have "pie chart" nodes coded as follows:

gene1: completely grey
gene2: completely red
gene3: completely black
gene5: two slices, 180°, one black, one grey
gene7: three slices, 120° each, one black, one grey, one red.
...

The functionality has been implemented recently, from what I understand. It is available by selecting "flexible slice number colouring" in the panel. Your node attribute file would then be prepared as follows:


ATTRIBUTE_NAME (class=java.lang.String)
gene1 = (k)
gene2 = (o)
gene3 = (k::o)
gene_i = (p::k::0)


Notice, however, that you'd still have the problem with the elliptical node shape: looks like in the current implementation you are limited to a round node shape for best results (using rectangles, ellipses etc would result in a pie-circle embedded in one of those shapes).

Also, if you're looking for proportionality between (continuous value) attributes and corresponding pie slice size, I think the plug in won't allow you to do that.

Apologies if this still does not answer your requirements.

Best,
G


On 24/08/11 16:31, Grimes Mark wrote:
Giuseppe

Thanks for that suggestion, I downloaded the 2.4.12 version of
Multicolor Nodes from SourceForge and this now works on Cy 2.8.1.

The graph I would like to achieve is a bit more complicated than the
capability of the plugin, unfortunately. I want each node to represent
by color the presence or absence of an attribute, so for example if only
two of four attributes are present I want a pie with two colored halves
instead of four quarters with two quarters blank, which is what the
plugin does. This can be done using pie() in R and RCytoscape - but I
still need to solve the problem of making the pie fit exactly into the
node shape ELLIPSE without a blank border around it.

Best wishes,

Mark
